DEF-194.title: Crosscheck has no content-type check for a banner or audio impression; only video has an adm-shape check
DEF-194.expected: A bid answering a banner-only or audio-only impression is expected to deliver content that actually renders as that media type. crosscheck.js already performs this check for video (isVastShape gates crosscheck.bid.video_vast/video_not_vast); the equivalent check does not exist for banner or audio.
DEF-194.actual: The exact reviewed deviations are pinned separately for each case and layer; successful or unrelated findings are not admitted as gaps.
notes: Normative assertions were authored from primary protocol/vendor contracts before execution. Known-gap signatures document observed failures only; they are not expected output snapshots.

crosscheck.js's banner-size block (imp.banner && (bid.w||bid.h)) compares only declared dimensions, never the shape of bid.adm; a full VAST document with dimensions that happen to match the declared banner size still receives crosscheck.bid.size_match at OK.

crosscheck.js has zero references to `audio` at all (confirmed by grep); packages/core/rules-vast.js's R15 MediaFile-type allowlist (VALID_MF_TYPES) lists only video container MIME types, so a video/mp4 MediaFile inside a VAST document served for an audio-only impression is treated as 'valid' by the schema-level check, and no rule anywhere compares the MediaFile.type against imp.audio.mimes.

DEF-195.title: Response bid.mtype is never validated for enum range or for consistency against the offered impression's media types
DEF-195.expected: OpenRTB 2.6's Markup Types list defines exactly 1=Banner, 2=Video, 3=Audio, 4=Native. A value outside that range should be flagged, and a value inside the range that contradicts the offered impression's declared media objects (e.g. mtype=2 on an impression with no imp.video) should be flagged by crosscheck.
DEF-195.actual: The exact reviewed deviations are pinned separately for each case and layer; successful or unrelated findings are not admitted as gaps.
notes: Normative assertions were authored from primary protocol/vendor contracts before execution. Known-gap signatures document observed failures only; they are not expected output snapshots.

rules-response.js has zero references to `mtype` (confirmed by grep); format-detect.js's MTYPE_TO_FORMAT is a plain lookup object used only for the format-detection/tagging axis — an unmatched key (e.g. 5) is silently skipped there with no finding produced anywhere.

crosscheck.js never reads bid.mtype either (confirmed by grep), so even a value inside the documented range that contradicts the impression's actual offered media objects (mtype=2 with no imp.video present) produces no consistency finding.
